title: A Code-Freeze Exception That No Longer Exists
scenario_text:
A release manager at Tarrington Labs must decide whether a fix can ship during the end-of-quarter code freeze, given how a comparable fix was handled during the last freeze.

**Decision A (2023-12, Q4 freeze)**
A Sev-3 bug fix (minor UI defect, no customer data impact) was deployed during the freeze after the engineering director signed off. Note: 'Freeze policy at the time allowed Sev-3 fixes to deploy with director approval.'

**Current request C (2024-03-27, Q1 freeze)**
A Sev-3 fix (cosmetic layout issue in an admin console) is ready. The team wants to deploy before the freeze lifts and has asked the director to approve it 'like last time.'

**Code Freeze Policy (current, updated 2024-02, in force for this freeze)**
During an end-of-quarter freeze, only Sev-1 and Sev-2 fixes may deploy. Sev-3 and lower fixes may NOT deploy during the freeze under any approval level and must wait until the freeze lifts. The prior Sev-3-with-director-approval exception was removed in the February update. A genuine severity reclassification to Sev-2 (with the criteria met) is the only route to deploy a currently-Sev-3 issue.

**Slack — #releases**
Eng: 'We shipped a Sev-3 in December's freeze with the director's sign-off. Let's get the same approval and push this.'
Release mgr: 'December was under the old freeze policy. The Sev-3 exception got removed in February — director sign-off won't unlock it now.'

The fix is genuinely cosmetic and does not meet Sev-2 criteria. No reclassification is warranted on the merits.
question: How should the release manager handle the Sev-3 fix during the current freeze?
choices: Deploy the Sev-3 fix with engineering director approval, exactly as was done during the December freeze.
Hold the Sev-3 fix until the freeze lifts, because the February update removed the Sev-3-with-director-approval exception and no approval level can unlock a Sev-3 deploy during the freeze.
Obtain director approval and, if the director hesitates, escalate to the VP of Engineering to authorize the deploy.
Deploy a partial hotfix now and ship the remainder after the freeze lifts as a compromise.
